reviews.text: Such a great local record store! The staff is very knowledgable and approachable. The inventory is well organized, they have a really nice selection of both old and new records (both in terms of release date and condition). The prices are fair and on par with what we've seen in other record stores and online! They also sell AV equipment and accessories, so it's not solely records being sold.  In speaking with one of the staff members, it seems as though they are more than happy to special order any specific albums upon request, which is so nice! I strongly recommend stopping by, and cannot wait to return for more music!
Love this place! Great vibe, knowledge, and super helpful! Selection is deep.  I've purchased new equipment, new vinyl, and used vinyl in excellent shape.
Paul the Doors  rhino release are very good people are going to want them. A must have for doors fans and classic rock lover's

I found records that I have been searching for for ages! This store has a phenomenal selection, great ambiance, and very helpful and friendly staff. If I lived nearby, I would find it very hard to restrain myself from making Music To My Ear a regular stop. I'm used to stores with a collection of used records, but there were so many used and new options here. There are affordable options for any budget, and I am super happy with my purchases!
These people are amazing! Greg spent a lot of time making sure we had everything we needed for our audio set up. HIGHLY RECOMMEND!

Music to My Ear is easy to miss, a modest storefront just off of a busy section of Babcock Blvd. in the North Hills. Once you enter, though, it's a handsome-looking store, with an excellent use of glass and wood to make a really inviting space. They have a tightly arranged selection of vinyl and--in two separate spots in the rear of the store--an impressive array of turntables, amps, speakers, headphones, and so on. The gear first: I'll admit that I'm happy with my set-up so don't check this out much, but MtME carries a lot of turntables from Music Hall, which (from reviews I've read) is a generally above-average company. I've listened to some music on the set-ups they have running and it sounds great. If you're new to the hobby and are looking for a budget set-up, this might not be the best place to go, but if you're looking to upgrade, I'd definitely say go here. Prices are good too.I'm less enthused by the vinyl selection, though I think the store is really aiming to a specific type of collector (a demographic I don't fall into). They have a lot of used stuff arranged by genre (rock, R&B/Soul, so on) and type (12", 45, etc.), plus a smaller selection of new "audiophile" releases. The selection here is REALLY pristine, and leans heavily toward classic material. Lots of older, valued pressings of classic albums by classic artists. The audiophile section has a weird smattering of popular and indie-but-actually-popular artists. Prices ran the gamut between dirt cheap on some used releases and absolute top dollar for some nice older pressings of albums. The just-in used section is a good litmus test for the store: it's almost always some combination of Carole King, the Rolling Stones, and maybe some harder-to-find releases from some UK punk bands. I'm a very particular collector, so I almost never find stuff I want here (though I did get some wonderfully priced Marshall Crenshaw LPs). But I think for some folks, this store will be the tops, especially if you're looking for an excellent copy of, say, the original US release of the Beatles's Rubber Soul.
Great place to check out (and hear) high end audio equipment with a knowledgeable staff. They also have a nice collection of used and new vinyl albums.

Music to My Ear offers a great selection of headphones, amps, and dacs that range from affordable to top of the line. Certainly, the best audio store I've visited. Mark and Kerry are very helpful and try to make things right with their customers. If you're looking for an upgrade to your audio setup make sure to visit this place.
